subject: MCNALLY: unexpected p95 jump on /v1/generate — coordinated triage & customer note
messages:
From: Jared Park <jared.park@mcnally.ai>

Cc: McNally Support <support@mcnally.ai>
Date: 2029-06-12T08:14:00Z
Subject: sudden p95 jump on /v1/generate in prod — seeing 3-4s

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing a sharp p95 increase on our main batch endpoint (/v1/generate) around 07:50 UTC — p95 jumped from ~700ms to ~3.8s and error rate slightly increased (0.3% -> 0.9%). This affects our checkout personalization pipeline; throughput dropped by ~25%.

I attached a short trace dump and a heatmap of latencies. Minimal changes on our side — no traffic spike, and request sizes are in the usual distribution. Can you confirm whether this is an infra-side or model/runtime issue? We need ETA for mitigation because this is customer-facing.

Attached: mcnally-p95-dump-20290612.log, trace-heatmap-20290612.png

Thanks,
Jared

Date: 2029-06-12T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: sudden p95 jump on /v1/generate in prod — seeing 3-4s

Quick findings from initial triage:
- Kernel scheduling and GPU utilization on the MCNALLY pool look normal (no >90% sustained).
- Observed intermittent KV-cache evictions on several hosts serving the pool between 07:48–08:10 UTC; eviction rate spiked correlating with the p95 jump. Cache hit-rate fell ~12%.
- A recent model rollout (small param-only tweak) was active on a subset of nodes 07:40–07:55 UTC. It should have been traffic-mirrored, but routing show a small percentage diverted for compatibility testing.

Hypothesis: rollout-induced cache warming penalty + small routing diversion caused synchronous backend misses, inflating p95 for requests that hit cold KV entries.

Immediate mitigations we can execute now:
1) Pause the partial rollout and revert the small param tweak across the test cohort (safe, quick).
2) Increase soft-prefix cache window and enable immediate local warmup for hot keys (config flip — risk low).
3) Add temporary conservative routing to prefer warmed host subset for MCNALLY traffic.

I can run 1+2 in the next 10–15m; recommend doing 3 after 1 is visible. Will also open JIRA-INF-1429 with traced spans.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Subject: Re: sudden p95 jump on /v1/generate in prod — seeing 3-4s

Jared — quick update and customer-facing summary below (short, copy-able). We’re executing mitigations now and will follow with a postmortem.

Customer note (draft):
Hi Jared — we’re seeing an increase in 95th percentile latency on /v1/generate impacting some requests. Engineering has identified that a small staged model rollout coincided with increased KV cache evictions which temporarily increased p95 for a subset of traffic.

Action taken: we have halted the staged rollout, increased local cache warmup settings for hot prefixes, and are routing McNally traffic to a warmed host subset to stabilize latency. Initial telemetry shows p95 trending back toward baseline. We will share a short postmortem with root cause, timeline, and protective actions within 48 hours.

ETA: stabilization in 10–30 minutes; full RCA within 48 hours.

If that reads OK I’ll send it from our support alias so it goes into your ticketing queue.

Attachments: attaching the two logs you sent for transparency.

— Soojin
